# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel the large button embossed “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” but I have no tactile information about the wires. I’m asking the Mute to provide the manual’s instructions and coordinate the Deaf’s visual observations before I act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. I cannot identify the wire contents. Please provide the manual instructions and have the Deaf report all bomb markings and wire colours.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, yellow light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

The Deaf reports display 0, a yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. I should pass these visual facts to the Mute and request the relevant manual rule; I still must not touch anything until the rule identifies a safe action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, yellow light, and wires: position 1 red, position 2 blue, position 3 green. What does the manual instruct?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled: ? ? ?. I cannot interpret the meaning. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

I still know only that the Mute sent three gestures; as Blind, I cannot identify them. No safe action follows from the bomb’s physical state alone. I need the Deaf to describe what those gestures mean or otherwise relay the manual’s rule aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute repeated the gestures ? ? ?. I cannot interpret them or the manual. Please wait for the mute's spoken instructions.

The Mute’s gestures are the only possible route for the manual’s contents, but the Deaf should not try to interpret them independently. The Mute can gesture the instruction, and the Deaf can report each gesture’s visual description aloud; I can then reconstruct and follow it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual instruction one symbol at a time. Deaf should describe each gesture aloud to me exactly, rather than interpreting it.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest signal was the single gesture ?. I cannot interpret it. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

The latest report still gives me no identifiable gesture or manual instruction. Since the Mute cannot speak, the Mute’s gesture must be relayed by the Deaf through a spoken physical description. I am asking the Mute to use ordinary, describable hand signs and the Deaf to describe them aloud rather than treating them as an instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use only ordinary describable gestures, one at a time. Deaf must speak a plain description of each gesture aloud so I can identify the manual instruction. Do not send an unexplained sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled ?, then ?. I cannot interpret these gestures. Bomb remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

The manual’s information is still not reaching me in an identifiable form. The Deaf can see the Mute’s gestures, but must describe their hand shapes in words; otherwise I cannot distinguish them. I will send the Deaf a clear request to relay descriptions rather than interpretations.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute just made a hand signal with thumb, index finger, and little finger extended and the other fingers folded. Your latest signal was a hand pointing directly outward. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

The Deaf has now successfully described the Mute’s latest gesture: thumb, index finger, and little finger extended, which identifies 🤟. This is only the gesture’s identity, not its meaning in the manual, so I still need the complete manual rule relayed as gesture descriptions. I will ask the Mute to send the rule in individually described gestures, and the Deaf to report each one.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The Deaf can describe your gestures. Send the relevant manual rule one gesture at a time, pausing between gestures, so the Deaf can report each hand shape to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute's latest gesture was ?: two fingers raised. Your latest gesture was ?: one finger raised.

The Mute’s latest gesture is identifiable as two raised fingers, likely the gesture for “2,” while the prior one used three extended fingers (thumb, index, little finger). This does not yet establish whether the manual calls for cutting wire 2 or another operation. I need the Mute to give an unambiguous action code, with the Deaf describing every gesture in order.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer using this exact code: first gesture means PUSH or CUT; if CUT, second gesture means wire 1, 2, or 3. Use one clear hand shape per item, and repeat the full code twice.")
wait()
```
